question.text: A Cat III AIF maintains multiple Series within the same Class of Units. Why does the Series NAV per unit differ across Series, even though they hold the same underlying portfolio?

answer.text: Custodian fees are charged only to the senior Series
SEBI requires a 10% haircut on later Series for dilution
Differential terms of subscription (fees, drawdown timing) allocated at series level cause Series Expenses and Series Net Assets to diverge
Each Series holds a different subset of the portfolio

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 14.12, Series NAV differs because differential terms of subscription (management fee %, incentive fee %, hurdle, drawdown timing) are allocated at the Series level. Series Expenses (esp. mgmt fees) are specific to each Series, while common fund expenses/assets/liabilities are allocated pro-rata to Opening Series NAV. Same portfolio, different fee drag = different NAV. **The Trap:** Option A invents a SEBI haircut rule. Option C misconceives 'series' as a portfolio segregation. Option D is fabricated. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-B touches series concept. XIX-C dives into the mechanics managers must operate — and the recent SEBI bar on 'priority distribution models' that privilege one class at the cost of another. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Maintain a 'series waterfall grid' updated at each close. When new money enters mid-life, new Series units are struck at current NAV — getting the opening NAV wrong creates permanent under/over-allocation to the new investor.
